24K likes, 144 comments - harman_fitness_mommy on May 24, 2026: "My TED Talk is out. ❤️

The link is in my bio I truly hope you watch it.

In the talk, I spoke about postpartum and the bounce-back culture  consuming mothers around the world . But while sharing those experiences, I kept thinking about something much deeper… about women, about silence, and about how easily so many lose themselves trying to hold everything together.

And today, that feeling hits even harder.

Our country is shaken by the heartbreaking loss of a young woman whose story has left all of us disturbed, emotional, and questioning so much about the reality many women live in every single day. 
This incident happened recently, after my TED Talk , but somehow the conversations still meet at the same truth.

How many women are silently suffering?
How many are taught to adjust until they disappear within themselves?
How many stay because they fear judgment more than unhappiness?

More than anything, I want every woman to remember this:

Please never lose yourself completely in the process of becoming someone’s wife, mother, or “perfect bahu.”

Be emotionally strong.
Be financially independent and above all 
Know your worth.🫶

Because independence is not ego it is dignity, safety, and strength.

If my TED Talk leaves you with one thought, let it be this: healing begins when a woman chooses herself too. 🤍

God bless ✨ 

#tedtalk #tedxtalks #tedx #motivation #ᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇᴘᴀɢᴇ".

posts.meta_description:
13K likes, 162 comments - harman_fitness_mommy on June 6, 2026: "83 kg ➡️ 56 kg

Everyone wants to know the secret.

The truth is, if there is ONE thing I would tell every woman trying to lose weight whether postpartum or not it is this:

Strength training is non-negotiable.

Over the years, I’ve watched people jump from one thing to another. Extreme diets. Endless cardio. Yoga. Pilates. Running. Not running. Detoxes. Challenges. Quick fixes.

But after more than a decade in fitness, and after going through two pregnancies and two major abdominal surgeries (both my babies were born via C-section), my opinion hasn’t changed.

Strength training remains the foundation.

This isn’t even my first postpartum transformation.

After my second baby, I lost the weight in just five months, and I give a huge amount of credit to strength training because it was the one thing I stayed consistent with. I trained throughout my pregnancy and, with proper medical clearance and recovery, I was back in the gym within five weeks postpartum.

The results strength training can create in your physique, metabolism, strength, confidence, and overall health are phenomenal.

But there is another reason this journey was successful:

A great coach.

People often think a coach just writes workouts and meal plans.

A good coach does much more.

They hold you accountable when motivation disappears.
They spot mistakes before they become habits.
They teach you about food instead of just restricting it.
They help you make better decisions consistently.
They guide you through setbacks.
And sometimes, they help you navigate the life stresses that are quietly sabotaging your progress.

Instead of spending hours searching Google for answers, you have someone who understands your body, your goals, and your journey.

Weight loss isn’t about finding the perfect diet.

It’s about finding a system you can trust, staying consistent, and doing the basics exceptionally well for a very long time.

No shortcuts.
No magic pills.
No hacks.

Just consistency, strength training, proper nutrition, accountability, and patience.

And trust me, the results will speak for themselves. ❤️

Coach @puneetbigguy 

#postpartum #weightloss #fatloss #coach".

posts.meta_description:
20K likes, 306 comments - harman_fitness_mommy on February 17, 2026: "Winning the Best Parent Fitness Influencer award 🏆 
for the second time is deeply emotional and incredibly meaningful to me. 

I want to extend my heartfelt gratitude to @kidsstoppress for not only recognizing my work, but for creating a platform that acknowledges the importance of fitness in parenting.

Having a dedicated category for parent fitness influencers speaks volumes. It empowers parents who are quietly and consistently dedicating their lives to becoming stronger - not just for themselves, but for their children. It also inspires so many other mothers and fathers to prioritize their health, showing them that their well-being matters too.

A very special thank you to Mansi Zaveri @mansi.zaveri for building this platform with such sincerity and vision. Your commitment to recognizing the contributions of parents, and the many roles we juggle while raising our children, creating content, and showing up every day, means more than words can express.

To my community this belongs to you as much as it does to me. Thank you for voting, for believing in me, for supporting me through this 10-year journey. It hasn’t always been easy, but your love, trust, and encouragement have kept me going.

Being seen. Being valued. Being trusted by other parents… that is the real award.

Thank you for this honor. 🤍

A heartfelt thank you to @sogoodindia for supporting and encouraging this beautiful category. I’ve personally been a huge fan of So Good for years, and it was truly special to stand there, receiving this recognition alongside a brand I genuinely believe in and trust. It made the moment even more meaningful and full circle for me. 🤍".

posts.meta_description:
12K likes, 112 comments - harman_fitness_mommy on September 17, 2026: "Ab bas mil Gaya na nazar mat lagao 🧿🤪

Coach @puneetbigguy  jokes apart read this below 👇 

Having a great coach is so much more than having someone tell you what to do.

Today, there is absolutely no shortage of fitness information. There are apps, websites, workout plans, YouTube videos, books you name it. You can find a workout for almost anything with just a few clicks.

But I think what truly changes the game is the human being behind the coaching.

A coach listens to you. A coach understands you. They know your struggles, your patterns, your limitations, your strengths and they adapt accordingly. They’re not just sending you a PDF and expecting you to figure it out on your own.

And especially for women, sometimes you’re not even looking for a solution. Sometimes you just need to vent. 😂

Because the person you train with consistently becomes so much more than your coach. They become your guide, your support system, sometimes even your friend. And your conversations inevitably go beyond fitness because life doesn’t exist in separate compartments.

And then there’s accountability.

When you know you have to go back to your coach and tell them what you did, what you ate, how you felt, whether you showed up it creates a completely different level of commitment. It’s not like buying an online plan, downloading it, and then having nobody notice whether you actually followed it.

There are a hundred ways to exercise today. There are endless plans and programs available.

But there is something very powerful about investing in a person who is invested in you.

Someone experienced enough to guide you, honest enough to challenge you, and present enough to listen to you.

And honestly, that relationship can make the entire experience of training not just more effective, but so much more enjoyable.

Because sometimes, the difference between having a workout plan and actually getting results is simply having someone who cares whether you show up.

#transformation #fitnesslife #fitness #coach #postpartumbody".
